about: The publisher's log on rfrmdwordlabs.com/editions/log (rfrmdwordlabs-web/tools/make_editions_log.py). One entry per update a reader is offered, newest first, keyed by the shelf id. Reader-facing: what is better, in plain words, no dashes.

mystery-of-the-secret-band.text: Read against the 1935 Saalfield printing. The list of the hotel's rooms and guests that Mary Louise copies into her notebook in Chapter 3 is back; it had dropped out of the earlier copy. No wrong words were found.

green-tent-mystery.text: Three short verses in Chapter 10 are back, Charlotte Ann's bedtime prayer among them; they had dropped out of the earlier copy.

pilgrims-progress.text: Paragraphs and punctuation now follow George Offor's edition of 1855: 37 paragraphs divided where he divided them, one joined, three breaks between stanzas restored, and 22 marks of punctuation corrected. Bunyan's words are unchanged.
The lines that open Part II are centred, as printed, and the marks that lead to the notes are shown.

Read against Offor's editions of 1855 and 1859: 30 typing errors corrected, and Bunyan's own words restored where they had been changed. The notes keep to Bunyan's own, and the life of Bunyan has been checked against its sources.

adventures-of-sherlock-holmes.text: Read against our own scan of the 1892 Harper printing: more than 1,100 corrections across the twelve stories. Misread figures and words are put right, conversation that had run together is divided as printed, paragraphs broken at a page turn are joined, stray spaces in the punctuation are gone, and the quotation marks are curly.
The closing page, How These Books Are Made, is plainer and says truly how the spelling is handled.

rare-jewel-of-christian-contentment.text: The spelling is brought up to date, so the book reads easily and sounds right when read aloud; Burroughs's own words are kept. Printer's slips are mended, the punctuation of the long sentences is made clearer, and two Scripture references are corrected: 1 Samuel 26:20 and Hebrews 2:10.
The closing page, How These Books Are Made, is plainer and says truly how the spelling is handled.

treasure-island.text: Read against the 1894 Scribner printing: some forty words that had gone wrong in transcription are put right, among them a few of the pirates' own turns of speech. The songs and rhymes are set line by line, as Stevenson printed them, the one footnote now sits at the end of its chapter instead of inside the story, the chapters are numbered so the voice reads them plainly, and every picture carries its caption in words. The spelling is now American, compound words are written as one (spyglass, campfire), and a few old words in the telling are given in ours; one word whose meaning has changed carries a small note giving Stevenson's own.

swiss-family-robinson.text: Read against Kingston's own 1891 printing: two passages missing from the last chapter, among them the father's farewell charge to his sons, are restored, and about a hundred small slips are put right. The quotation marks are set properly, some older spellings are brought up to date so the book reads and sounds right (today, tomorrow, kayak), Juno's epitaph is set as verse, and the chapters are numbered so the voice reads them plainly. Compound words are written as one (shellfish, pineapple) and old words are given in ours (there for thither); where a word has changed its meaning, as terrific has, a small note gives Kingston's own.
